STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r10.claim: The sūrah repeatedly contrasts believers with disbelievers, using questions about whether knowers and non-knowers are equal and affirming that God’s guidance cannot be undone.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r10.anchor: the sūrah juxtaposes the believers and the disbelievers throughout

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r8.claim: God assures the Prophet that He alone protects him; no one can withhold God's mercy or avert harm, and the decision belongs to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r8.anchor: God is sufficient for his protection; no one can deprive him of God’s mercy if it has been ordained from Him

IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read بكاف عبده as a plural; the remaining readers use the singular.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائى ﴿ بكاف عبده ﴾ جماعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r6.speaker: قريش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r6.claim: Quraysh threatened to set their idols against Muhammad to make him insane or bring him harm unless he stopped insulting their gods and them; the verse was revealed in response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r6.anchor: قالت قريش: لئن لم ينته محمد عن تعييب آلهتنا وتعييبنا، لنسلطها عليه فتصيبه بخبل وتعتريه بسوء، فأنزل الله: أليس الله بكاف عبده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r7.claim: The interrogative over a negation seeks confirmation: God does protect His servant, and calling him God’s servant greatly honors the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r7.anchor: والهمزة الداخلة على النفي للتقرير، أي هو كاف عبده، وفي إضافته إليه تشريف عظيم لنبيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r8.claim: The majority read the singular عبده as the Messenger of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: عبده، وهو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر ومجاهد وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r9.claim: These readers have the plural عباده, referring to the prophets and obedient believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر، ومجاهد، وابن وثاب، وطلحة، والأعمش، وحمزة، والكسائي: عباده بالجمع، أي الأنبياء والمطيعين من المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r10.claim: The beings by which Quraysh threatened the Prophet are idols; the story says Khalid broke al-Uzza’s face with an axe despite her attendant’s warning of her power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r10.anchor: ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه: وهي الأصنام. ولما بعث خالدا إلى كسر العزى، قال له سادنها: إني أخاف عليك منها، فلها قوة لا يقوم لها شيء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r11.claim: Their threat is mockery because the idols cannot bring benefit or harm; a similar threat was made by the people of Hud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r11.anchor: وفي قوله: ويخوفونك، تهكم بهم لأنهم خوفوه بما لا يقدر على نفع ولا ضرر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r12.claim: Another reading connects بكافي to عبده by annexation; the form يكافي عباده is a present verb from كفى with عباده as its object and can be an emphatic form of sufficing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p204#2/r12.anchor: وقرىء: بكافي عبده على الإضافة، ويكافي عباده مضارع كفى، ونصب عباده فاحتمل أن يكون مفاعلة من الكفاية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r1.claim: The reading can also be understood as a reciprocal form meaning God repays His servants, as in the verb يجازي for يجزي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون مهموزا من المكافأة، وهي المجازاة، أي يجزيهم أجرهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r2.claim: If God suffices His servant, fearing the idols is pointless and false.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r2.anchor: ولما كان تعالى كافي عبده، كان التخويف بغيره عبثا باطلا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r3.claim: Because the passage includes the guided and the astray, it says that God is the agent of all of it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p205/r3.anchor: ولما اشتملت الآية على مهتدين وضالين، أخبر أن ذلك كله هو فاعله

RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r1.claim: Razi presents the closing statements as the decisive conclusion: reminders and proofs benefit only those whom God singles out for guidance and success.
RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r1.anchor: هذا الفضل لا ينفع والبينات إلا إذا خص الله العبد بالهداية والتوفيق

RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r3.claim: Razi's Ashʿarī associates cite the paired guidance statements for their doctrine that God creates acts and wills all events.
RAZI-FULL:v26p245/r3.anchor: أصحابنا يتمسكون في مسألة خلق الأعمال وإرادة الكائنات بقوله

STUDYQURAN:39:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r1.claim: The opening asks whether God sufficed Muhammad as He had sufficed the prophets before him.
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r1.anchor: Did not God suffice Muhammad, as He sufficed the prophets before him?

STUDYQURAN:39:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r2.claim: The idolaters thought that invoking their idols’ displeasure and wrath could influence the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r2.anchor: their idols’ displeasure and wrath will somehow influence the Prophet (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:39:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r3.claim: His servant can mean any believer: God suffices those who worship only Him and rely solely upon Him.
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r3.anchor: can also be understood to mean any believer, meaning that God suffices for anyone who worships only Him and relies solely upon Him (IK)

STUDYQURAN:39:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r4.claim: The assurance follows the analogy in 39:29: monotheism frees the believer from divided masters and scattered aspirations, since God provides all that is needed.
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r4.anchor: In this sense, it follows upon the analogy of v. 29

STUDYQURAN:39:36/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r5.claim: Those who do not believe and trust God are left astray, without a way, guide, or protector, and are losers.
STUDYQURAN:39:36/r5.anchor: The one who does not believe and trust in God is allowed to go astray and has no way

BURSEVI:v8p82/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r1.speaker: داود
BURSEVI:v8p82/r1.claim: In an anecdote, David explains that he eats a morsel without knowing whether it is lawful or unlawful, expressing scrupulous concern about its source.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r1.anchor: هذه الكسرة آكلها ولا أدري أمن حلال هي أم من حرام

BURSEVI:v8p82/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد أبو الخير
BURSEVI:v8p82/r2.claim: Asked what truth is and how to reach God, Abu Sa'id says truth is God's trust in His servants, in which the lower self has no share; the self cannot reach the Real.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r2.anchor: (وشيخ أبو سعيد أبو الخير قدس سره را در مجلس سؤال كردندكه).

BURSEVI:v8p82/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r3.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p82/r3.claim: The Prophet tells Muadh to purify his religion, for a little deed will then suffice him.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r3.anchor: قال عليه السلام لمعاذ رضي الله عنه : "يا معاذ

BURSEVI:v8p82/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p82/r4.claim: The interrogative hamza over negation affirms and establishes God's sufficiency; sufficiency fills need and achieves the desired end.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r4.anchor: أدخلت همزة الإنكار على كلمة النفي

BURSEVI:v8p82/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p82/r5.claim: God suffices Muhammad against his enemies and supports him against them, consoling him; the wording may encompass everyone who realizes true servitude.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r5.anchor: هو تعالى كاف عبده محمدا صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أمر من يعاديه

BURSEVI:v8p82/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v8p82/r6.claim: Some great Sufis read the servant as one who worships God and believes in Him, or one realizing the divine identity from which divinity begins.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r6.anchor: وعن بعض الكبار أليس بكاف عبده

BURSEVI:v8p82/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p82/r7.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says God suffices His servant against everything, while nothing can suffice the servant against God; even the treasures of the heavens do not divert the Prophet from beholding God.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : أن الله كافف عبده عن كل شيء

BURSEVI:v8p82/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r8.speaker: عرائس البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p82/r8.claim: The Arā'is al-Baqli sees a gentle reproach: God asks whether servants imagine He will abandon His care and protection; no one dares oppose one under His eternal regard.

BURSEVI:v8p82/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r9.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p82/r9.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says whoever abandons choice and scheming, returns sincerely to God in every state, and seeks help only from Him will be sheltered by divine acceptance and freed from all concerns.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r9.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : من تبرأ من اختياره واحتياله

BURSEVI:v8p82/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r10.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p82/r10.claim: A hadith says God suffices the worldly and afterlife concerns of one who wakes with a single concern.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أصبح وهمومه هم واحد

BURSEVI:v8p82/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82/r11.speaker: عبد الواحد زيد
BURSEVI:v8p82/r11.claim: Abd al-Wahid Zayd predicts that Utba al-Ghulam, absorbed in watching the Creator, will enter; when asked, Utba says he saw no one although his route was the crowded marketplace.
BURSEVI:v8p82/r11.anchor: (عبد الواحد زيدرا كفتند هيج كس را دانى كه در مراقبت خالق جنان مستغرق

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r1.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r1.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq says no beauty exceeds the rich person's humility toward the poor, except the poor person's disregard of the rich through sufficiency in God and His care.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r1.anchor: وقال السيد جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه : ما رأيت أحسن من تواضع الأغنياء للفقراء

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r2.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says anyone not satisfied with his Lord's sufficiency after this verse belongs among the doomed.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر رحمه الله : من لم يكف بربه

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says that after this verse, looking to, hoping in, fearing, or coveting anything among creatures strips away the marks of servitude.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : رفع جلاجل العبودية من عنقه

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r4.claim: The polytheists frighten Muhammad with their idols, claiming that because he insults them they will kill, madden, or physically harm him.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r4.anchor: أي : المشركون {بالذين من دونه} ؛ أي : بالأوثان

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r5.claim: Some exegetes say the verse was revealed once about the Prophet and again about Khalid ibn al-Walid, just as al-Fatiha was revealed in Mecca and Medina.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التفسير : إن هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r6.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r6.claim: A report says Arab idolaters worshipped a tree with a demon called al-Uzza beneath it; sent to uproot it, Khalid ignored their threats, killed the demon, and the Prophet declared al-Uzza would never be worshipped again.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r6.anchor: ونزولش در حق خالد بن الوليد آنست كه قومى از مشركان عرب درختى را

BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r7.claim: God misguides one from the straight way and sound understanding so that he forgets God's sufficiency and protection and fears what cannot harm or benefit.
BURSEVI:v8p82#2/r7.anchor: ومن يجعله دالا عن الطريق القويم والفهم المستقيم حتى غفل عن كفايته تعالى

BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r1.claim: No guide remains to direct the person to what is good.
BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r1.anchor: فما له من هاد} يهديه إلى خير ما

BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r3.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says seeing good or evil as coming from other than God is misguidance, and the true guide or misleader is God, whom none can countermand.
BURSEVI:v8p82#3/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى أن رؤية الخير والشر

TAB-FULL:v20p211/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r1.claim: The polytheists threaten Muhammad with their idols, claiming they will harm him for rejecting and criticizing them; God will suffice him.

TAB-FULL:v20p211/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r2.claim: Qatada recounts that Muhammad sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to smash al-ʿUzza; its keeper warned him, but Khalid struck the idol's nose with an axe.

TAB-FULL:v20p211/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r3.claim: Al-Suddī identifies those invoked besides God as the gods Quraysh worshipped.

TAB-FULL:v20p211/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise says they threatened Muhammad with the gods worshipped besides God.
TAB-FULL:v20p211/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه}

TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.claim: The open-ended promises that God answers supplication and suffices His servant reinforce that ordinary causal expectations do not limit what God brings about.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.anchor: كما يدل عليه أيضا إطلاق قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r3.claim: “Those besides Him” refers to the polytheists’ gods, while “His servant” refers to the one praised in the preceding verses, primarily the Prophet.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r3.anchor: المراد بالذين من دونه آلهتهم من دون الله على ما يستفاد من السياق

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r4.claim: The question seeks affirmation: God is sufficient for His servants, reassuring the Prophet against threats involving their idols and implicitly promising protection.

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r5.claim: The implicit promise of sufficiency is stated explicitly in 2:137.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r5.anchor: كما صرح به في قوله فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم البقرة 137

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r6.claim: The two reciprocal statements are universal maxims; naming God rather than using a pronoun is an apparent noun in place of a pronoun.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r6.anchor: جملتان كالمتعاكستين مرسلتان إرسال الضوابط الكلية

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r7.claim: Their placement after the promise of sufficiency signals that the idol-threateners will not find guidance or attain their aims against the Prophet, whom God has guided.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى أن هؤلاء المخوفين لا يهتدون بالإيمان أبدا

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r8.claim: God’s might and retributive power explain the maxims: He punishes those who deny truth and persist in unbelief, and no one can overcome Him or mislead a servant He guides.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r8.anchor: فإن عزته وكونه ذا انتقام يقتضيان أن ينتقم ممن

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r9.claim: The explanation implies that divine misguidance is retribution and punishment, not an initial act of leading someone astray.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r9.anchor: وفي التعليل دلالة على أن الإضلال المنسوب إلى الله تعالى

TABRISI:39:36-38/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:39:36-38/r1.claim: The Kufan readers except ʿĀṣim, together with Abū Jaʿfar, read the plural عباده; the remaining readers read the singular عبده.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وأبو جعفر بكاف عباده على الجمع والباقون عبده على التوحيد

TABRISI:39:36-38/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:39:36-38/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the singular reading with the following clause: God is sufficient for you while they frighten you.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r2.anchor: حجة من قرأ عبده ويخوفونك فكأن المعنى ليس الله بكافيك

TABRISI:39:36-38/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:39:36-38/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the plural as God sufficing His prophets, as He protected Abraham from fire, Noah from drowning, and Jonah from his plight, and so will suffice Muhammad.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ عباده فالمعنى أليس الله بكاف عباده الأنبياء كما كفى إبراهيم النار

TABRISI:39:36-38/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:36-38/r7.claim: After promising the truthful and those who affirm truth, God assures them He will suffice them despite enemies who target and harm them; here the servant is Muhammad.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r7.anchor: لما وعد الله سبحانه الصادق والمصدق عقبه بأنه يكفيهم وإن كانت الأعداء تقصدهم وتؤذيهم

TABRISI:39:36-38/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r8.speaker: قتادة والسدي وابن زيد
TABRISI:39:36-38/r8.claim: Qatāda, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd say the unbelievers frightened Muhammad with the idols they worshipped, claiming their gods would destroy him.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r8.anchor: كانت الكفار تخوفه بالأوثان التي كانوا يعبدونها عن قتادة والسدي وابن زيد

TABRISI:39:36-38/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:36-38/r9.claim: An alternative report says that when Khālid went to break al-ʿUzzā on the Prophet's order, people warned him of the idol's might; he struck it and declared God had humiliated it.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r9.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما قصد خالد لكسر العزى بأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:39:36-38/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:36-38/r10.claim: One whom God misguides through disbelief and sins from the path to Paradise has no guide who can lead him there.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r10.anchor: أي من أضله الله عن طريق الجنة بكفره ومعاصيه

TABRISI:39:36-38/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:36-38/r11.claim: Another explanation means that once a person has strayed from truth, no one can call that person a guide.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن من وصفه بأنه ضال إذ ضل هو عن الحق

TABRISI:39:36-38/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:36-38/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:36-38/r12.claim: A further explanation is that God withholds increases in guidance from the person, leaving no one to provide that increase.
TABRISI:39:36-38/r12.anchor: وقيل: من يحرمه الله من زيادات الهدى فليس له زائد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r1.claim: The servant God suffices is Muhammad; God supports him and protects him from his enemies.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r1.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلوات الله عليه، ينصره ويكفيه أمر من يعاديه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r2.claim: The idolaters threatened Muhammad with their idols, saying that because he insulted them they would harm him; despite worshipping idols, they admitted God is the Creator.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:36/r2.anchor: يخوفونك بأوثانهم، يقولون: إنك لتعيبها، وإنها لتصيبنك بسوء

ELMALILI:39:32-41/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:32-41/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:32-41/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as asking whether God is not sufficient for His servant, while they frighten the Prophet with those besides Him; whoever God leads astray has no guide.
ELMALILI:39:32-41/r1.anchor: Allah kuluna kâfî değil mi? Durmuşlar da seni ondan beridekilerle korkutuyorlar, her kimi ki Allah şaşırtır artık ona hidâyet edecek yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r1.claim: Tafsir accounts say Quraysh pagans tried to frighten Muhammad, saying that although he spoke ill of their idols, they feared the idols would strike him or make him ill.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r1.anchor: Tefsirlerde belirtildiğine göre Kureyş putperestleri, Hz. Peygamber’e, “Sen putlarımız hakkında kötü sözler söylüyorsun ama biz putlarımızın seni çarpmasından, hastalandırmasından kaygı duyuyoruz” diyerek onu korkutmaya çalışırlardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r2.claim: Verse 36 reassures the Prophet and marks such beliefs as deviation; verse 37 says no power can divert those guided by God. God backs His Prophet and followers against enemies and punishes those who stray, assuring steadfast believers of His help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:36/r2.anchor: 36. âyetle bu hususta onun gönlünün rahatlatılması amaçlanmış

BURHAN:v3p83/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p83/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p83/r1.claim: The preposition ب can be added to the subject of كفى; “كفى بالله” means “Allah suffices.” Al-Zajjaj explains it as كفى taking on the sense of اكتفى, which the author finds sound.
BURHAN:v3p83/r1.anchor: وقال الزجاج دخلت لتضمن كفى معنى اكتفى وهو حسن

BURHAN:v3p83/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p83/r7.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v3p83/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAsfur says bāʾ is exceptionally augmentative in a rare, non-analogical construction such as “بقادر”; the author identifies the intended verse and cites its parallel without bāʾ as evidence.
BURHAN:v3p83/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور في المقرب 9 وتزاد في نادر كلام لا يقاس عليه

BURHAN:v4p115/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p115/r1.speaker: الزجاج
BURHAN:v4p115/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the preceding construction by invoking the prohibition on swearing by other than God; the author calls this objection strange because that prohibition concerns created beings.
BURHAN:v4p115/r1.anchor: رده الزجاج بالنهي عن الحلف بغير الله وهو عجيب فان ذلك على المخلوقين

SULAMI:v2p199#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p199#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p199#3/r1.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir says whoever is not content with God’s sufficiency after this declaration is among the doomed.
SULAMI:v2p199#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : من لم يكتف بربه بعد قوله : ﴿ أليس الله بكاف عبده ﴾ فهو في درجة الهالكين

SULAMI:v2p199#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p199#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p199#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says whoever afterward looks to, hopes from, fears, or covets any created being has cast off the bond of servanthood.
SULAMI:v2p199#3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : خلع حبل العبودية من عنقه من نظر بعد هذه الآية إلى أحد من الخلق أو رجاهم أو خافهم أو طمع فيهم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r1.claim: A familiar likeness can be compressed into metaphor: calling a praised man a lion conveys courage, while calling a woman the sun conveys beauty.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r1.anchor: وجدت في دليل الحال وفي العرف ما يبين غرضك إذا يعلم إذا قلت رأيت أسد وأنت تريد الممدوح أنك قصدت وصفه بالشجاعة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r2.claim: A complex likeness cannot be compressed into metaphor when its point emerges only after several clauses explain the comparison.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r2.anchor: لا سبيل إلى معرفة المقصود من الشبه فيه إلا بعد ذكر الجمل التى يعقد بها التمثيل فإن الأستعارة لا تدخله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r3.claim: In the example of the man who is like night, saying only “night sheltered me” either means darkness or misses the intended point that the fugitive cannot escape his reach.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p211/r3.anchor: إما أن تحذف الصفه وتقتصر على ذكر الليل مجردا فتقول إن فررت أظلنى الليل وهذا محال

FARRA:v2p418/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p418/r11.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وأبو جعفر المدني
FARRA:v2p418/r11.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab and Abu Jaʿfar al-Madanī read ʿibādihi, plural; other readers have ʿabdihi, singular.
FARRA:v2p418/r11.anchor: قرأها يحيى بن وثاب وأبو جعفر المدني (أليس الله بكاف عباده) على الجمع

FARRA:v2p418/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p418/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p418/r12.claim: Quraysh threatened that their gods would harm the Prophet for criticizing them; this prompted the reassurance that God suffices for His servant.
FARRA:v2p418/r12.anchor: وذلك أن قريشا قالت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

FARRA:v2p419/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p419/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p419/r1.claim: The singular reading refers to Muhammad; those reading the plural include earlier prophets, whose peoples also threatened them, as in Shuʿayb's story. Both readings are sound.
FARRA:v2p419/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله (أليس الله بكاف عبده) محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، فكيف يخوفونك بمن دونه

SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r1.claim: The common reading has singular عبده.

SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r2.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r2.claim: The two Kufan readers use plural عباده for prophets and followers.
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r2.anchor: والأخوان " عباده " جمعا وهم الأنبياء وأتباعهم

SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r3.claim: A further reading has بكافي عباده in annexation, with يكافى as verb and عباده as object.
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r3.anchor: وقرئ " بكافي عباده " بالإضافة. و " يكافى " مضارع كافى

SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r4.claim: The reciprocal form may mean the simple verb, as نجازي means نجزي, with emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r4.anchor: ثم المفاعلة هنا تحتمل أن تكون بمعنى فعل نحو: نجازي بمعنى نجزي

SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r5.claim: Alternatively, it derives from hamzated يكافئ for recompense, with softened hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون أصله يكافئ بالهمز، من المكافأة بمعنى يجزيهم، فخفف الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r6.claim: ويخوفونك is circumstantial or a new sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:39:36/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا؛ إذ المعنى: أليس كافيك حال تخويفهم إياك بكذا

ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r1.claim: Those worshipped beside God include false deities, living or dead saints, and abstract powers or values such as wealth, status, racial preeminence, and self-sufficiency.
ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r1.anchor: This relates not merely to false deities, but also to saints alive or dead, and even to certain abstract concepts

ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r2.claim: Asad says the godless magnify the need to heed these imaginary powers and frighten themselves and others with fears of practical harm if they are ignored.
ASAD-NOTES:39:36#n39/r2.anchor: The godless always stress the supposed necessity of paying attention to all these imaginary forces and values

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r1.claim: The author argues that the ba attached to the predicate of negated laysa does not reinforce negation; it reverses it into an asserting, binding affirmation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r1.anchor: الباء فيها لم تؤكد النفي، بل هي تنقُضه وتجعله تقريراً وإثباتاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r1.claim: Across these interrogatives about laysa-negated propositions, the negation is overturned into definite affirmation; the ba consistently accompanies the predicate.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r1.anchor: النفي في هذه الآيات جميعاً قد انتقض وخرج إلى تقرير باتَّ وإثبات حاسم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r2.claim: Although rhetoricians recognize that interrogatives can shift into assertion or other functions, the ba's regular presence here contributes to the declarative force.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r2.anchor: ومن حيث اطرد اقتران الخبر فيها بالباء، تعين أن يكون لهذه الباء أثرها في الدلالة البيانية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r3.claim: Without ba, examples such as 'Are you not heedless?' or 'Is not morning near?' can remain genuine questions or convey rebuke, warning, mockery, or expectation, unlike the Qur'anic forms under discussion.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p189/r3.anchor: احتمل الاستفهام أن يكون على معناه الأصلي من طلب الفهم، وأن يخرج إلى التوبيخ أو التنبيه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r4.claim: Section IV turns to assuring the Prophet against threats tied to false deities and summarises the themes of verses 36–52.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r4.anchor: The succeeding verses sound an assurance to the Prophet (sws): he should tell those people who are intimidating him through their deities

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r5.claim: The Prophet should know that only the Creator of the heavens and earth can harm or benefit him, so the deities used to intimidate him cannot do so.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r5.anchor: except for this Lord Who is the creator of the heavens and the earth no one can harm or give benefit to him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r1.claim: The polytheists threatened the Prophet with their deities’ wrath for preaching monotheism; God alone can protect and sustain him, and nothing harms without His permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r1.anchor: These verses sound assurance to the Prophet Muh@ammad (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r2.claim: Fearing harm independent of God’s permission implies that God is insufficient to protect and sustain a person, which is disbelief and polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r2.anchor: this obviously is disbelief and polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r3.claim: The statement that God guides or misguides people rebukes the polytheists’ ignorance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p554/r3.anchor: express rebuke on the ignorance of the polytheists.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p555/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p555/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p555/r1.claim: God’s established practice leads these people astray because of their deeds, so none can guide them; this reassures the Prophet not to heed arrogant opponents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p555/r1.anchor: God has led them astray and those who are led astray by God can be guided by none.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p95/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p95/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p95/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read عباده in the plural; the remaining readers read عبده in the singular, which the source links to the following singular address ويخوفونك.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p95/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: بكاف عباده [الزمر/ 36] جماعا.

NASHR:v2p362#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p362#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p362#2/r4.claim: The word هاد has a separate note on pausing according to the written rasm.

NASHR:v2p362#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p362#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p362#2/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read عباده in the plural; the others read عبده in the singular.
NASHR:v2p362#2/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف، عباده بألف على الجمع

QIRAAT-ER:39:36:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:36:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:39:36:5#1/r1.claim: The plural reading changes His servant to His servants, broadening the claim of sufficiency from one servant to the servant community.
QIRAAT-ER:39:36:5#1/r1.anchor: Canonical plural reading changes singular His servant to His servants, broadening the sufficiency claim

QIRAAT-ER:39:36:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:36:20#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:39:36:20#1/r1.claim: The pause or continuation variant permits final yāʾ realization at a recitation boundary while preserving the active participle.
QIRAAT-ER:39:36:20#1/r1.anchor: Canonical pause/continuation variant preserves the active participle while allowing final yāʾ realization

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p173#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p173#2/r1.speaker: رجل
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p173#2/r1.claim: An unnamed man told Maʿmar that the polytheists threatened the Prophet: stop insulting their gods or they would order them to afflict him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p173#2/r1.anchor: قال لي رجل إنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لتكفن عن شتم آلهتنا أو لنأمرنها فلتخبلنك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r1.claim: The interrogative emphatically denies that God fails to suffice His servant: the certainty of His sufficiency is so clear none can deny or hesitate over it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r1.anchor: إنكار ونفي لعدم كفايته تعالى على أبلغ وجه كأن الكفاية من التحقق والظهور بحيث لا يقدر أحد على أن يتفوه بعدمها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says “His servant” means the Messenger; the following threat by those besides God supports this, since the Quraysh refer to their idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r2.anchor: على ما روي عن السدي وأيد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r3.speaker: قريش
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r3.claim: The Quraysh warned the Prophet that their idols might drive him mad or harm him for disparaging them; another report has them demanding he stop insulting their gods or suffer harm, after which the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r3.anchor: وقد روي أن قريشا قالت له عليه الصلاة والسلام : إنا نخاف أن تخبلك آلهتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r4.claim: Alternatively, “His servant” is generic, with the Prophet included foremost; the plural reading supports this and is interpreted as covering prophets and believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r4.anchor: أو الجنس المنتظم له عليه الصلاة والسلام انتضاما أوليا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r5.claim: On the singular reading, followers are also intended: God suffices the Prophet and believers in the necessities of religion and worldly life and protects them from unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r5.anchor: ومن أنه داخل في كفاية مهمي الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام وأتباعه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r6.claim: The passage connects the denunciation of those who lie about God and deny truth with the recompense of the truthful believer, then extends God's favor to His servant.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r6.anchor: لدلالته على أنه تعالى يكفي نبيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مهم دينه ودنياه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر ومجاهد وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r7.claim: Abu Jafar, Mujahid, Ibn Waththab, Talha, al-Amash, Hamza, and al-Kisai read “His servants” in the plural; other readings make it genitive after “sufficing” or use the verb “yukafi” with an accusative object.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r7.anchor: وقريء ( بكافي عباده ) بالإضافة و ( يكافي عباده ) مضارع كافي ونصب ( عباده )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r8.claim: The “yukafi” reading may derive from sufficiency, like “yujari” for “yajri,” and be more emphatic through its intensive form; Alusi finds this likely given the Quran's frequent use of that sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r8.anchor: وهو أبلغ من كفى لبنائه على لفظ المبالغة وهو الظاهر لكثرة تردد هذا المعنى في القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r9.claim: The alternate form may instead be hamzated and derive from mukafaah, meaning requital.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون مهموزا من المكافأة وهي المجازاة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r10.claim: The requital reading fits the preceding rewards and the Prophet's focus: God will surely recompense His beloved servant, while the idol-threats warn of a supposed counter-recompense; still, the common reading's meaning of sufficiency is stronger.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p5/r10.anchor: نعم لا ننكر أن معنى الكفاية أبلغ كما هو مقتضى القراءة المشهورة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p6/r1.claim: Whoever God misguides becomes heedless of His sufficiency for His servant and fears things that cannot benefit or harm; such a person has no guide to lead him to good.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r3.claim: The singular “His servant” refers to Muhammad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r3.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read “His servants” in the plural, referring to the prophets whom their peoples targeted with harm; God protected them, as in 40:5.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي: "عباده" بالجمع يعني: الأنبياء عليهم السلام، قصدهم قومهم بالسوء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r5.claim: The idolaters threatened Muhammad with harm from their idols if he did not stop insulting their gods, including derangement or madness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r5.anchor: وذلك أنهم خوفوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معرة الأوثان. وقالوا: لتكفن عن شتم آلهتنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r6.claim: Whomever God leads astray has no guide.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p120#2/r6.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r7.claim: The interrogative denies the negation, emphatically affirming that God suffices His servant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r7.anchor: استفهام إنكار للنفي مبالغة في الإثبات

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r8.claim: The servant may mean the Messenger of God, or the wording may be general; the latter is supported by the reading His servants, explained as the prophets.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r8.anchor: والعبد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويحتمل الجنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r9.claim: The threateners are Quraysh, who said they feared their idols would harm the Prophet because he criticized them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r9.anchor: يعني قريشا فإنهم قالوا له إنا نخاف أن تخبلك آلهتنا بعيبك إياها

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r10.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r10.claim: A report says the Prophet sent Khalid to break al-Uzza; its custodian warned Khalid of the idol's force, so the threat to Khalid counted as a threat to the Prophet who sent him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r10.anchor: وقيل إنه بعث خالدا ليكسر العزى فقال له سادنها أحذركها

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r11.claim: God misguides one who overlooks His sufficiency and fears what cannot benefit or harm; such a person has no guide to right conduct.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:34-36/r11.anchor: حتى غفل عن كفاية الله له وخوفه بما لا ينفع ولا يضر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r11.claim: After the unbelievers deny the truth and threaten the Prophet with their idols, the verse’s emphatic question affirms God’s sufficiency and denies that He fails to protect His servant.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r11.anchor: حسن كل الحسن قوله مقرا للكفاية غاية الإقرار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r12.claim: The servant is the one devoted purely to God, without associating anything with Him, whom God aids against his opponents until His religion prevails and he needs no other protector.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r12.anchor: أي الخالص له الذي لم يشرك به أصلا كما تقدم في المثل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r13.claim: Trust in God’s sufficiency does not rule out using worldly means: God may connect effects to them or render them ineffective, and using means best accords with His wise ordering of the world.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r13.anchor: وهاذ لا ينافي السعي في الأسباب مع اعتقاد أنها بيد الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r14.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر
BIQAI-FULL:v6p447/r14.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Jaʿfar read عباده in the plural, meaning the Messenger and his followers.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r1.claim: Their threat echoes the people of ʿĀd, who told Hūd that some of their gods had afflicted him; the author says later feminizing the idols will add to their humiliation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r1.anchor: وسيأتي التعبير عنهم بالتانيث زيادة في توبيخهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r2.claim: God alone determines guidance and misguidance; this consoles the Prophet against grieving over those he cannot guide and rejects the Qadariyya position.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r2.anchor: فقال مخففا عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في إذهاب نفسه عليهم حسرات دامغا للقدرية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r3.claim: God may make one cause bring misguidance to some, warranting punishment, and guidance to others, bringing blessing; He can still guide some of the present opponents if He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p449/r3.anchor: جعل شيئا واحدا سببا لضلال قوم ليكون ضلالهم في الظاهر علة للنقمة

DURR-FULL:v7p229/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies those besides God used to frighten the Prophet as idols.
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه} قال: الأوثان

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r1.claim: Qatādah says the threats concerned idols and reports that when Khālid ibn al-Walīd went to break al-ʿUzzā, its custodian warned him; Khālid then smashed its nose with an axe.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه قال : بالالهة قال : بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خالد بن الوليد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās transmits Prophetic counsel to obey and rely on God, ask and seek help only from Him, and know that people cannot harm or benefit beyond what God decrees; patience brings relief and ease follows hardship.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3251#3/r2.anchor: حديث قيس بن الحجاج ، عن حنش الصنعاني ، عن ابن عباس مرفوعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r4.claim: The preceding parable of the one master and contentious partners provokes idolaters to defend their gods and threaten the Messenger, leading into this reassurance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r4.anchor: لما ضرب الله مثلا للمشركين والمؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r5.speaker: قريش
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r5.claim: Al-Kashshaf and al-Qurṭubi report that Quraysh feared their gods would harm the Prophet because he insulted them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r5.anchor: أن قريشا قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives an account similar to the report that Quraysh threatened the Prophet with harm from their idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r6.anchor: وفي ( تفسير ابن عطية ) ما هو بمعنى هذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p12/r7.claim: The threat resembles Abraham's people calling for him to be burned and urging support for their gods.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r1.claim: God, whom the Prophet alone worships, suffices against the polytheists and their false gods; the opening reassurance also hastens their dismay and the Prophet's comfort.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r2.claim: The underlying order would put their threats first and God's protection after; the wording is rearranged for effect. Alternatively, the first sentence is independent and the threat clause circumstantial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r2.anchor: وأصل النظم : ويخوفونك بالذين من دون الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r3.claim: Calling the Prophet عبده instead of using direct address directs the statement to the polytheists; the omitted object of كاف is their harm, and the question rebukes their belief that idols can harm him without a protector.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r3.anchor: ووقع التعبير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالاسم الظاهر وهو { عبده } دون ضمير الخطاب لأن المقصود توجيه الكلام إلى المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r4.claim: The servant is certainly the Prophet by the following address; his designation as God's servant honors him and assures that God will not hand him over to enemies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r4.anchor: والمراد ب { عبده } هو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لا محالة وبقرينة و { يخوفونك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r5.claim: The shift from third-person reference to direct address is iltifāt, focusing the threat sentence specifically on the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r5.anchor: والخطاب في { ويخوفونك } للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو التفات من ضمير الغيبة العائد على { عبده }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r6.claim: Those beside God are idols; the rational relative form is conventional for them, and the omitted relative clause means that the polytheists took or worshipped them apart from God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r6.anchor: عبر عنهم وهم حجارة بموصول العقلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r7.speaker: البيضاوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r7.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī gives as a revelation occasion Khalid ibn al-Walid's mission against al-ʿUzzā: its keeper warned him, then Khalid broke the idol; threats to Khalid were meant for the Prophet, making the verse Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r7.anchor: تفسير البيضاوي ) أن سبب نزول هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur says the Medinan occasion does not fit the context and suggests the story may only illustrate a familiar idol threat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p13/r8.anchor: ولعل بعض من قال هذا إنما أراد الاستشهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r1.claim: Most readers have the singular عبده; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Abū Jaʿfar, and Khalaf read plural عباده, referring to the Prophet and believers whom God protects.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r2.claim: The intervening statement portrays their misguidance as deeply rooted in their nature and generations, so attributing its creation to God implies it is exceptionally hard to uproot.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r2.anchor: قصد من هذا الاعتراض أن ضلالهم داء عياء لأنه ضلال مكون في نفوسهم وجبلتهم قد ثبتته الأيام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r3.claim: Denying that they have a guide is a figurative way to deny that they attain guidance; Ibn Ashur links the formulation to al-Aʿrāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r3.anchor: وأريد من نفي الهادي من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r4.claim: Both this wording and al-Aʿrāf negate any guide; من makes generic negation explicit here, while لا plus an accusative noun does so there, a rhetorical variation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r4.anchor: والآيتان متساويتان في إفادة نفي جنس الهادي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r5.claim: Putting له before هاد emphasizes their condition: they trust powerless idols to harm the Prophet despite their evident impotence and ignore the true Lord's power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r5.anchor: وتقديم { له } على { هاد } للاهتمام بضميرهم في مقام نفي الهادي لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r6.claim: The emphasis differs from al-Aʿrāf, where misguidance is failure to consider the heavens and earth, less egregious than fearing idols; the following verse assures that the guided remain firm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p14/r6.anchor: بخلاف آية الأعراف فإن فيها ذكر إعراضهم عن النظر في ملكوت السماوات والأرض وهو ضلال دون ضلال التخويف من بأس أصنامهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r1.claim: Exegetes say Meccan polytheists warned Muhammad that his criticism of their gods might bring him harm; this verse was revealed in response.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r1.anchor: ذكر المفسرون أن مشركي مكة قالوا يا محمد ما تزال تذكر آلهتنا وتعيبها فاتق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r2.anchor: والمراد بعبده هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read “His servants” in the plural, referring to the prophets whom their peoples targeted; God will protect Muhammad as He protected them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي عباده على الجمع وهم الأنبياء لأن الأمم قصدتهم بالسوء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو عمران الجوني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r4.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and Abu ʿImran al-Jawni read بكافي with an explicit yāʾ and عبده with the specified kasras, without an alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r4.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو عمران الجوني بكافي مثبتة الياء عبده بكسر الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب وأبو العالية وأبو الجوزاء والشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r5.claim: Ubayy, Abu al-ʿAliya, Abu al-Jawzaʾ, and al-Shaʿbi share that reading but retain the alif in عباده.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وأبو العالية وأبو الجوزاء والشعبي مثله إلا أنهم أثبتوا الألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو جعفر وشيبة والأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r6.claim: Al-Sulami, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, and al-Aʿmash read بكاف with tanwin and عباده in the plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو جعفر وشيبة والأعمش بكاف بالتنوين عباده على الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو رجاء العطاردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Abu Rajaʾ al-ʿAtaridi read يكافي and عباده in the plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو رجاء العطاردي يكافي بياء مرفوعة قبل الكاف وياء ساكنة بعد الفاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184#2/r1.claim: Those besides God are the idols they worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p184#2/r1.anchor: أي بالذين يعبدون من دونه وهم الأصنام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r1.claim: God suffices the servant who worships Him and relies on Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r1.anchor: يعني أنه تعالى يكفي من عبده وتوكل عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r2.claim: Some read the word in the plural, His servants, instead of His servant.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r3.claim: The Prophet said success belongs to one guided to Islam who has sufficient livelihood and is content with it; al-Tirmidhī graded the report ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r3.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد الأنصاري؛ أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r4.claim: The polytheists threaten the Messenger with the idols and deities they invoke besides God, out of ignorance and error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r4.anchor: يعني: المشركين يخوفون الرسول ويتوعدونه بأصنامهم وآلهتهم التي يدعونها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r5.claim: God is invincible: one who relies on Him cannot be overpowered, while He takes vengeance on those who disbelieve, associate partners, and defy His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p100/r5.anchor: منيع الجناب لا يضام، من استند إلى جنابه ولجأ إلى بابه، فإنه العزيز الذي لا أعز منه، ولا أشد انتقاما منه

JISHUMI:v8p6066/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r3.speaker: المشركون
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r3.claim: The polytheists allegedly asked whether Muhammad feared their gods, which might harm or unhinge him for insulting them.
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r3.anchor: قيل: إن المشركين قالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أما تخاف آلهتنا حيث تعيبها بأن تصيبك بسوء أو تخبلك

JISHUMI:v8p6066/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r4.claim: In the account, Muhammad ordered Khalid to smash al-ʿUzza; after warnings, Khalid struck its nose with an axe and declared its humiliation.
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r4.anchor: فأمر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خالدا بكسر العزى، فقالوا: إياك يا خالد فبأسها شديد، فضرب خالد أنفها بالفأس

JISHUMI:v8p6066/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r5.speaker: المشركون
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r5.claim: A second report says they threatened to order their gods to make Muhammad insane unless he stopped insulting them.
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r5.anchor: وروي أنهم قالوا: لتكفن عن شتم آلهتنا أو لنأمرنها حتى تخبلك

JISHUMI:v8p6066/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r6.claim: Only those who abandon reason fear inanimate idols; through imitation, they attribute benefit and harm to them, as ʿAd did with Hud’s god.
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r6.anchor: من لا يستعمل عقله فهو والبهيمة سواء، فهو مع كونه جمادا اعتقدوا فيه النفع والضر تقليدا كقول عاد لهود - عليه السلام

JISHUMI:v8p6066/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r7.claim: The comparison invokes 11:54, where ʿAd says one of their gods has afflicted Hud with harm.
JISHUMI:v8p6066/r7.anchor: كقول عاد لهود - عليه السلام -: (إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء)

JISHUMI:v1p443/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p443/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p443/r6.claim: He cites this negated question as an example of wording that invites acknowledgment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r1.speaker: بعضهم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r1.claim: Some read singular “His servant,” referring to Muhammad, whom God protects from polytheists.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r1.anchor: في قراءة بعضهم , يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم يكفيه الله المشركين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r2.speaker: الباقون
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r2.claim: The remaining readers read plural “His servants,” referring to the prophets.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r3.speaker: الكلبي والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi say they threatened that idols would harm the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم كانوا يخوفونه بأوثانهم يقولون تفعل بك وتفعل , قاله الكلبي , والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r4.claim: Alternatively, they intimidated him with their own threats.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p127/r4.anchor: الثاني : يخوفونه من أنفسهم بالوعيد والتهديد

MUJAHID:v2p558#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p558#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p558#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the beings used to frighten the Prophet as the idols worshipped besides God.
MUJAHID:v2p558#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ﴾ يعني يخوفونك بالأوثان التي يعبدون من دون الله عز وجل

MUQATIL:39:36-38/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r1.claim: God suffices His servant Muhammad and protects him from his enemy.
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r1.anchor: { أليس الله } يعنى أما الله { بكاف عبده } يعنى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يكفيه عدوه

MUQATIL:39:36-38/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r2.speaker: كفار مكة
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r2.claim: The Meccan idolaters threatened that their gods al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt might make Muhammad mad or deranged.
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r2.anchor: وذلك أن كفار مكة، قالوا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن نخاف أن يصيبك من آلهتنا اللات والعزى ومناة جنون أو خبل

MUQATIL:39:36-38/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r3.claim: Whoever God leads astray from guidance has no one to guide him to Islam.
MUQATIL:39:36-38/r3.anchor: { ومن يضلل الله } عن الهدى { فما له من هاد } [آية: 36] يهديه للإسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza applied to a negative affirms and confirms that God suffices.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r1.anchor: أدخلت همزة الانكار على كلمة النفي فأفيد معنى اثبات الكفاية وتقريرها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.claim: Ḥamza reads the plural عباده, referring to the prophets and believers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.anchor: عباده حمزة وعلى أي الأنبياء والمؤمنين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.claim: In the singular reading, God's servant is Muhammad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ عبده ﴾ أي محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r4.claim: This resembles God's assurance that He has sufficed the Prophet against the mockers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.claim: Quraysh said they feared their idols would make the Messenger mad or harm him because he criticized them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r5.anchor: وذلك أن قريشا قالت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انا نخاف أن تخبلك آلهتنا وانا نخشى عليك مضرتها لعيبك إياها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.claim: Anyone God leads astray has no guide.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p55#3/r6.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.claim: Whoever God abandons has no guide; this statement refutes the Qadariyya and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.anchor: أي من خذله فلا مرشد له. وهو يرد على القدرية وغيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.speaker: ابن كثير وابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin pronounce the final yāʾ when pausing on hād in both locations; the other readers omit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.anchor: ووقف ابن كثير وابن محيصن على قوله: «هاد» في الموضعين بالياء، الباقون بغير ياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r1.claim: The yāʾ in kāfin is dropped before the following tanwin; although it could be restored at pause, it stays dropped to match connected pronunciation, while some Arabs say kāfī at pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r1.anchor: حذفت الياء من «كاف» لسكونها وسكون التنوين بعدها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r2.speaker: عامة القراء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r2.claim: The common reading is singular, referring to Muhammad, whom God protects from the threats and plots of the polytheists.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r2.anchor: وقراءة العامة { عبده } بالتوحيد يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the plural ʿibādahu, referring either to the prophets or to the prophets and their believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { عباده } وهم الأنبياء أو الأنبياء والمؤمنون بهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the common singular reading because the next clause addresses the Prophet directly.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r4.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد قراءة الجماعة لقوله عقيبه: { ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه }

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r5.claim: The singular may be generic, like al-insān in the cited verse, making the first reading include the plural sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون العبد لفظ الجنس

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r6.claim: God suffices against the harm of idols, with which the polytheists frightened believers; Abraham made the same argument in the cited verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r6.anchor: والكفاية شر الأصنام، فإنهم كانوا يخوفون المؤمنين بالأصنام

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r7.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r7.claim: Al-Jurjani says God suffices His believing servant through reward and His unbelieving servant through punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r7.anchor: وقال الجرجاني: إن الله كاف عبده المؤمن

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r8.claim: They threatened the Prophet with harm from idols, saying that unless he stopped speaking against them they would maim or hurt him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r8.anchor: وذلك أنهم خوفوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مضرة الأوثان، فقالوا: أتسب آلهتنا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r9.claim: Qatada reports that Khalid ibn al-Walid went to break al-ʿUzza with an axe; its caretaker warned him, but Khalid smashed its nose.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: مشى خالد بن الوليد إلى العزى ليكسرها بالفأس

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r10.claim: The warning to Khalid also counts as a threat to the Prophet because the Prophet had sent Khalid.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r10.anchor: وتخويفهم لخالد تخويف للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه الذي وجه خالدا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r11.claim: The threat also includes frightening the Prophet with their numbers and strength, as in the cited verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r11.anchor: ويدخل في الآية تخويفهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكثرة جمعهم وقوتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r12.claim: The statement that one whom God misguides has no guide was explained earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:36-37/r12.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
